pr_title: mixedversion: alllow tests to indicate minimum supported version
pr_body:
This commit introduces the `MinimumSupportedversion` test option the
mixedversion framework. This option is expected to indicate the
minimum version of CockroachDB that should be running for the test to
run properly. When not set, this version will default to
`OldestSupportedVersion`, which is the oldest version of CockroachDB
still actively supported.

When running an upgrade test with the `mixedversion` framework, we no
longer will schedule user hooks while the cluster is upgrading from
versions older than this minimum supported version. This stops us from
running our tests in exceedingly old versions (especially in release
branches), which should reduce flakes and the likelihood that we will
"rediscover" bugs already fixed.

Note the the cluster might still be bootstrapped from older,
unsupported versions even after this change; this ensures that the
functionality tested works as expected even in clusters created using
older system schemas.

This commit also removes some similar logic in the
`backup-restore/mixed-version` roachtest; that test's behaviour should
now be automatically supported by the framework as the default.

Fixes: #116431

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/117794)

Taking a short break from mutators work to introduce this change, which will reduce test failures in old/unsupported releases, which are unlikely to be novel bugs we would be interested in fixing.

Mixed-version tests on this branch pass (the cdc failure is expected and also happens on master):

https://teamcity.cockroachdb.com/viewLog.html?buildId=13558028&buildTypeId=Cockroach_Nightlies_RoachtestNightlyGceBazel&tab=buildResultsDiv

Mutators work will continue once this PR lands.

@msbutler Looks potentially related to some not-so-recent changes you made in this area in e8bd19754af3. Although the backport for that was also a little while ago.  Perhaps we've just gotten lucky with randomness inside this test.

We are trying to set this cluster setting on a version before it was introduced:

```
[mixed-version-test/5_run-maybe-set-custom-cluster-settings] 08:24:18 runner.go:326: mixed-version test failure while running step 5 (run "maybe set custom cluster settings"): pq: unknown cluster setting 'backup.restore_span.target_size'
test random seed: -6048320362005410752

                                    n1           n2           n3           n4
released versions                   v21.2.17     v21.2.17     v21.2.17     v21.2.17
logical binary versions             21.2         21.2         21.2         21.2
cluster versions before failure     21.2         21.2         21.2         21.2
cluster versions after failure      21.2         21.2         21.2         21.2
```

I could patch this test to handle errors from unknown cluster settings.

But also, @renatolabs It looks like the 23.1 version of this test runs upgrades from releases  well outside of our support window:
```
mixed-version test plan for upgrading from "v21.2.17" to "v22.1.22" to "v22.2.17" to "release-23.1":
```
 Is there a good reason for this? If not, could we bump the min binary used in this test to 22.2?

> Is there a good reason for this?

Not really, the framework is just not aware of the branch it's running on. By default it will go through up to 3 upgrades so that's why it started all the way in 21.2. I've been meaning to add an option to allow tests to say "never bootstrap in a version earlier than X". I'll try to get it done in the coming days.

review_comments:
That would allow the case where the minimum supported version and the current version differ only on patch/prerelese, i.e., they are part of the same release series. This means that this "upgrade" would not involve running migrations or changing the cluster version.

Since everything else in `mixedversion` is designed around upgrading from one series to the next, I felt like it's best to disallow this scenario at this moment.
Makes sense; maybe the error message below could be made more precise in case the difference comes down to patch versions.
Changed error to say `minimum supported version should be from an older release series than current version`.
Not immediately clear if this list may contain duplicates?

There are no duplicates (if there were, that would be an internal bug in the planner).

`allUpgrades` returns a list of all setup upgrades, followed by the test's upgrades. These run in order. An upgrade can either be run during setup or during "test" time, along with user functions.

I added a note about this in the comments, hopefully it makes this clearer.
Nit: maybe `addHooks`, since there isn't any explicit scheduling here, we're merely adding them as (planned) steps.

I'm not a huge fan of `addHooks` because `add` is a bit generic. I understand that this is not scheduling in the OS sense (moving something from ready to "run"); `schedule` here was meant more according to this definition:

> to plan something for a particular time
> 
> https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/schedule

which I would argue is what this function is doing.

The planner is explicitly designed to not run anything, so hopefully "schedule" isn't too confusing. That said, I was trying to come up with a better name and nothing felt much better (`planHooks` was the best I could come up with). Let me know if you would still prefer that, I can make the change.
Yep, it's fine as is, plus it's internal documentation. So, I should really RTFM :)
